Every question in quiz.json tests a point about the target of the change: The skill ships as one plugin tree that Claude Code, Factory Droid, and Codex all read: a session-start hook runs quizgate sync, a PreToolUse guard denies an agent's git push --no-verify and core.hooksPath changes, and an installer adds the plugin to every harness on PATH and trusts the Codex hooks.
Every question sits at design altitude: the problem the change solves, the shape chosen, the alternatives, and what it makes easy or hard next, above function names and flags
No question asks about these incidental parts of the change: the JSON fields of plugin.json; the selftest cases; the timeout values in hooks.json; the exact JSON-RPC calls of codex-trust-hooks
Every wrong option of a single or multi question is a plausible misreading of the change, not filler
Each question's key_points state what a correct answer must cover, at the same altitude as the question
When quiz.json has two or more questions, the last one applies several points of the change to one new case the change does not spell out
